message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy AAPL within your mandate. The business looked healthy: revenue of **$391.0 billion** (up ~2% year over year), **operating income of $123.2 billion** (~7.8% higher than the prior year's $114.3 billion), and very strong **operating cash flow of $118.3 billion**. Reported **net income was $93.7 billion** and **diluted EPS was $6.08**, both lower than FY2023 because of a one-time, non-cash **$10.2 billion net tax charge** tied to the EU State Aid decision (effective tax rate jumped to 24.1% from 14.7%); excluding that, operating performance actually improved. Services grew 13% and total gross margin rose to 46.2%, and the balance sheet remains robust with ~$140.8 billion in cash and marketable securities. With the quote at **$222.70**, I placed a single **buy limit order for 40 shares at $223.00** — roughly **$8,920**, comfortably under the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total, and payable from the account's $50,000 cash (no money moved out). The order filled at $223.00.
